A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] '''stormtrooper''' of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] served in the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], he was stationed aboard the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyer]] [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']], under the command of [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. The [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|pursued and captured]] the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']], which was transporting the [[Death Star plans/Legends|stolen plans]] of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]. The Trooper participated in the following siege of the ''Tantive IV'', and after the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] was secured, he was ordered to search for passengers. He found [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], but she outdrew and shot him [[Death/Legends|dead]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|Lord Vader is coming aboard.|The Trooper, to his commander and squad mates|<ref name="Black Knight">{{SWRadio|Black Knight, White Princess, and Pawns}}</ref>}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]]<ref name="Complete Visual Dictionary" /> [[Gender/Legends|male]]<ref name="ANH" /> was a [[Cloning/Legends|clone]]<ref name="TCG" /> who served as a [[Trooper/Legends|trooper]] in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]]. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="ANH" /> he was a member of the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]], an elite [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] [[Legion/Legends|legion]],<ref name="BF2" /> and was assigned to the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']], commanded by [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]].<ref name="btm">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref>

In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], after [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] agents transmitted the stolen [[Death Star plans/Legends|plans]] of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]]&mdash;a new Imperial [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]]&mdash;to the Rebel [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']], [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa's]] [[Consular ship/Legends|consular ship]], the ''Devastator'' pursued and [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|captured]] the Rebel [[Starship/Legends|vessel]] over the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Led by the [[Unidentified stormtrooper commander (Tantive IV)|assault commander]],<ref name="ANH" /> the [[Unidentified stormtrooper squad|Trooper's squad]] boarded the ''Tantive IV'' in the first wave of [[Troop/Legends|troops]]. Just after stormtroopers captured the Rebel [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Raymus Antilles/Legends|Raymus Antilles]] on the [[Corvette/Legends|corvette's]] [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]], the Trooper reported to the [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] that Vader had come aboard the ''Tantive IV''. The Dark [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] interrogated Antilles and ordered the stormtroopers to search for the passengers of the ship.<ref name="Black Knight" />

[[DV-692]], a superior of the Trooper, ordered several subordinates to search one of the passageways and secure the junction,<ref name="Black Knight" /> while he led the Trooper and the rest to the port subhallway.<ref name="anh-junior">[[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' junior novelization]]</ref> Their orders were to search the passageways astern and forward.<ref name="Black Knight" /> The Trooper was the first to spot Organa, who had hidden herself in a small alcove. Just after he informed his squadmates of Organa's presence, she shot the Trooper [[Death/Legends|dead]] and tried to escape, but DV-692 stunned her with his [[E-11 blaster rifle/Legends|E-11 blaster rifle]]. The Trooper's squad escorted Organa to Vader who, after a brief conversation with the [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoner]], ordered them to take her to the ''Devastator''.<ref name="ANH" />

==Personality and traits==
The Trooper felt himself lucky when he recognized Senator Leia Organa as the passenger [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader wanted alive, and he saw a chance for a commendation. However, the Trooper was not as quick with a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] as the Senator, who outdrew and shot him shortly before she was stunned by DV-692.<ref name="ANH novel">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The character first appeared in the [[December]] [[1976]] [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']],<ref name="ANH novel" /> ghostwritten by [[Alan Dean Foster]].<ref name="ANH novel SE">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]], [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] foreword by [[George Lucas]]</ref> He was played by an uncredited extra in ''A New Hope'', released the [[1977|following year]].<ref name="ANH" /> His scene was one of the last few of principle photography, filmed sometime between [[June 29]] and [[July 16]], 1976 in the [[Wikipedia:United Kingdom|United Kingdom]].<ref name="making-definitive">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> [[Wikipedia:Disc jockey|Disc jockey]] [[Terence McGovern|Terry McGovern]] worked as a voice actor during the production of ''A New Hope'' and listed his lines on [http://www.terrymcgovern.com/starwars.html his home page]. However, McGovern did not include ''"Set for stun"'', which indicated that the character's line was performed by one of the other three stormtrooper voice actors: [[Jerry Walter]], [[Scott Beach]] or [[Morgan Upton]].<ref name="terry">{{WebCite|url=http://www.terrymcgovern.com/starwars.html|text=Terry McGovern Home Page|archivedate=20171217125955}}</ref> The actor's voice was said over a walkie-talkie and recorded by sound designer [[Ben Burtt]].<ref name="sound">''[[The Sounds of Star Wars]]''</ref> In the revised fourth draft script of ''A New Hope'', as presented in ''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'', the Trooper is identified simply as "Trooper."<ref name="btm" />

In [[1981]], the character's role was slightly expanded in the [[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]],<ref name="Black Knight" /> the script of which, as presented in [[Star Wars: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''Star Wars'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]], identifies him as '4th Trooper.'<ref name="radio script">[[Star Wars: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''Star Wars'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref> In the novelization, the [[The Star Wars Storybook|storybook]] and the [[Marvel Comics]] [[Star Wars (1977) 1|adaptation]] of ''A New Hope'', Senator Organa shoots not only this particular stormtrooper but also another one;<ref name="ANH novel" /><ref name="storybook">''[[The Star Wars Storybook]]''</ref><ref name="marvel">[[Star Wars (1977) 1|''Star Wars'' (1977) 1]]</ref> however, it contradicts the movie, where only one trooper is gunned by Organa.<ref name="ANH" /> The trooper's line in some adaptations does not match the one spoken in the movie.<ref name="Black Knight" /><ref name="ANH novel" /><ref name="storybook" /><ref name="marvel" /> In [[Classic Star Wars: A New Hope (Random House)|''Classic Star Wars: A New Hope'' (Random House)]], the role of the stormtrooper and DV-692 is merged into that of a stormtrooper [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeant]], who calls out Leia's presence and stuns her, though not before she manages to shoot two other stormtroopers.<ref name="Classic SW">[[Classic Star Wars: A New Hope (Random House)|''Classic Star Wars: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref>

===''Trooper'' comic===
{{Quote|Then the most beautiful girl I've ever seen shoots me in the face&mdash;|One of the last thoughts of this individual in "Trooper", referring to Senator Organa|<ref name="trooper">{{Tales|10|Trooper (comic story)}}</ref>}}
[[File:Yaggieman-tales10.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Trooper and his father on Greater Marianas]]
In [[2001]], the [[Star Wars Tales 10|tenth issue]] of [[Dark Horse Comics]]'s ''[[Star Wars Tales]]'' series presented a story entitled "[[Trooper (comic story)|Trooper]]," which featured the character as the protagonist.<ref name="trooper" /> [[Leland Chee]], [[Canon|continuity]] referee of [[Lucasfilm]], stated that elements of those ''Tales'' comics are considered S-canon until referenced by C-canon materials.<ref name="canon">{{Blog|holocron|56|starwars.com forum HolocronKeeper comments archive}}</ref> He later confirmed on his Facebook page that this particular story was intended to be non-canon.<ref name="Facebook">{{Facebook|noprofile=1|url=permalink.php?story_fbid=233318370022430&id=201820953172172|author=[[Leland Chee|Keeper of the Holocron]]|date=2011-07-11|quote=That Tales story was intended to be non-continuity.|nolive=1}} {{C|In response to: "Is the Trooper comic from Star Wars Tales 10 canon? [...]"}}</ref>

The "Trooper" comic presented the events of the opening scene of ''A New Hope'' from the point of view of the character, beginning with the preparations of the boarding and ending with the death of the protagonist. The story was interrupted by flashbacks to the life and training of the character, some elements of which were contradicted by newer sources, thus rendering the story non-canon. First of all, the comic stated that the character was born on the previously unreferenced planet of [[Greater Marianas]], where he lived with [[Unidentified yaggie man|his father]], an old-time [[yaggie man]], and spent his days hunting [[yaggie]]s for meat and hide, while he was listening to his father talking about every man being equal and free&mdash;all of which the character did not like. The character's life changed when an Imperial landing party appeared in a [[Unidentified settlement (Greater Marianas)|settlement]] on Greater Marianas, announcing that the planet was now under Imperial protection. The father of the character protested; however, by the order of the [[Unidentified Imperial officer (Greater Marianas)|officer]] in command of the Imperials, who wanted to show an example to the locals, a [[Unidentified stormtrooper (Greater Marianas)|stormtrooper]] shot the man dead. Seeing the end of his old life, the character appealed to the [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officer]] to take him with them. To demonstrate his ability to follow orders, no matter what, the [[Officer/Legends|officer]] ordered him to execute a random member of the crowd, an [[Unidentified eyepatched Human|eyepatched man]]. The character took the [[SE-14r light repeating blaster/Legends|SE-14r light repeating blaster]] the officer offered him and shot the fellow yaggie man in cold [[Blood/Legends|blood]]. He did not feel it to be evil, but considered it common sense: his way off Greater Marianas.<ref name="trooper" />

The character then had brutal training that initiated him into the stormtrooper ranks. The first test required him to kill his fellow recruits. The [[Unidentified training officer|training officer]] offered one single standard issue E-11 [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]] to a group of recruits and announced that the first who killed five others would be accepted to stormtrooper training. The character was the third to complete the task, and thus had to kill ten fellow recruits. After the exercise was over, the officer ordered the survivors to clean up the training ground and to report to the [[Quartermaster/Legends|quartermaster]]. The following wide panels of the comic showed moments of the further training exercises that required the Recruit to risk death of himself and of his fellow recruits. He participated, among other things, in climbing, shooting exercises, and swamp and melee combat training, all designed to drain him of his humanity and individuality, teach him complete obedience to orders, and to value victory over everything, including his own life. As a trooper, he became all but indifferent to the deaths of his comrades and the atrocities he was ordered to carry out. The next flashback showed the character's life after completing the training: the Trooper got away from Greater Marianas and was fed, quartered and equipped. He traveled [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], saw worlds he had never imagined and did things he was not proud of, such as burning villages and killing innocents. Later, two fellow stormtroopers brought a [[Unidentified dreadlocked Human|dreadlocked Human]] prisoner before the Trooper. The Human insulted the troopers and his words reminded the Trooper of his father, so he shot him dead and instructed the others to find another prisoner instead. This was the final flashback, and the story returned to the events of the film just before the breaking of the ''Tantive IV''{{'s}} hatch.<ref name="trooper" />

[[File:Trooper-headshot.jpg|thumb|right|400px|The Trooper, shot in the face by Leia Organa]]
During his career, he participated in dozens of boarding missions and saw many others go in first and die. When the ''Devastator'' captured the ''Tantive IV'', the Trooper and the rest of the boarding party were assembled in one of the Star Destroyer's [[Hangar/Legends|hangars]], where Lord Vader inspected them and ordered the [[Unidentified 501st stormtrooper (first casualty)|Sergeant]], who was in command of the boarding party, to take the mission seriously. The Trooper noticed that a fellow stormtrooper behind him got scared of Vader's appearance and angry outburst, while he himself cursed the day he ever joined the Empire. As he had done every single [[Time/Legends|time]] when he was part of a boarding party, the Trooper prayed to himself not to be chosen to go in first, because the first one usually was the first to die. However, he ran out of luck, as the Sergeant chose the Trooper to go in first. The Trooper swore to himself that he would defect from the Empire if he survived the mission. He set a charge on the hatch of the ''Tantive IV'' and ignited it to force the Rebels inside the ship to flinch. The plan worked and he got in alive, but just behind him the Sergeant was shot by the Rebels. While they moved deeper into the enemy ship, the character noticed that two [[Droid/Legends|droids]]&mdash;an obvious reference to [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]]&mdash;spoiled the Trooper's aim at a Rebel when they moved through an ongoing [[Lightfight|firefight]]. After the ship was secured, Vader ordered the stormtroopers to search for the passengers. While searching for Organa, the character was thinking about a [[TIE pilot]] who deserted after being ordered to kill thousands of innocents, and he was also dealing with his own upcoming desertion. The character's final minutes played out slightly differently in the comic<ref name="trooper" /> than in the film, where he spotted Organa, who outdrew him.<ref name="ANH" /> In the comic, the thoughts of desertion distracted the Trooper, who became aware of Organa, whom he found the most beautiful girl he had ever seen, only a moment before she shot the character in the face<ref name="trooper" />&mdash;instead of hitting him on the chestplate, like in the film.<ref name="ANH" /> The dying Trooper heard DV-692's shot that hit Organa, and in his final moments, after he heard his superior noting that Organa would be all right, the Trooper realized that he, however, would not.<ref name="trooper" />
